sourceFile: Diocese of Missouri Prayer Cycle, all four 2026 quarterly PDFs ("Diocese of Missouri Prayer Cycle -- First/Second/Third/Fourth Quarter 2026"), fetched directly from the download links on https://diocesemo.org/resources/worship.
notes: The source page (https://diocesemo.org/resources/worship) currently publishes all four 2026 quarterly Cycle of Prayer PDFs (Jan-Mar, Apr-Jun, Jul-Sep, Oct-Dec), so this file covers the full calendar year (52 Sundays, January 4 - December 27, 2026) rather than only the third quarter noted in this corpus's own pre-fetch research note -- that note appears to have gone stale between when it was written and this ingestion.

Each week's source paragraph names four subjects in a fixed order: a Diocese of Missouri congregation (or, twice, a diocesan-wide ministry), a congregation/institution of the companion Diocese of Puerto Rico, a province/church of the Anglican Communion, and a region of the Armed Forces and Federal Ministries cycle of prayer (a nationwide, alphabetically-rotating list of U.S. states/territories and their military/VA installations that the diocese reprints verbatim into its own weekly text, beginning this year). All four are transcribed as this file's own weekly subjects, per this corpus's per-source-document convention; the companion-diocese, Anglican Communion, and Armed Forces items are recorded as `category` subjects (none is a Missouri congregation), per this task's guidance.

Each subject line in the source begins with a fixed formulaic lead-in ("In our Diocese of Missouri, we pray for...", "In our companion Diocese of Puerto Rico, we pray for...", "In the Anglican Communion, we pray for...", "In the Armed Forces and Federal Ministries [cycle of prayer], we pray for...") and frequently inserts the filler phrase "the people and ministry of" before the actual subject name. Both are stripped as non-substantive lead-in text; everything after them is preserved verbatim (including typos). Where stripping left the remaining text starting mid-sentence in lower case, only the first letter was capitalized to read as a standalone name (e.g. "our chaplains..." -> "Our chaplains..."); no other wording was changed.

Diocese of Missouri congregation entries print a parenthetical founding year (or two years separated by a slash, e.g. "(1874/1890)" for a merged parish) immediately after the congregation's own name, then continue the same sentence naming clergy and their roles. The founding year and clergy detail are both recorded in that subject's `note` field (e.g. "(1872). David, their Rector; ...") rather than folded into `name`, matching this corpus's existing convention for clergy detail (see episcopal-nebraska-2026.json); `name` and `place` hold only the congregation's own name and town/city.

June 14 and June 21, 2026 name diocesan-wide ministries ("our Diocesan Campus Ministries and all chaplains"; "our diocesan staff") rather than a specific congregation, and are recorded as `category` subjects with no `place`.

September 27, 2026 is the one week all year whose Diocese of Missouri paragraph never states the named congregation's town/city (confirmed by rendering the source PDF page as an image and checking visually, not just the extracted text) -- "Episcopal Church of the Holy Communion (1869)", with named clergy, but no "in [City]" phrase anywhere in that paragraph. Because this schema requires a non-empty `place` for a `parish` subject and none is printed to transcribe, this one subject is recorded as `category` (name only, founding year/clergy in `note`) instead of fabricating a location.

Preserved source typos/oddities, transcribed verbatim rather than corrected: "Pastoral Universitariaz" (companion-diocese entries, April 5 and July 5 -- likely "Pastoral Universitaria"); a duplicated boilerplate clause "...for the people and ministry of for the people and ministry of St. Mark's Episcopal Church..." (March 8) and "...we pray for the people and ministry of for Christ Episcopal Church..." (November 8) -- in both cases the duplication falls entirely within the stripped lead-in text and so does not appear in the transcribed `name`; "in in Arizona" doubled preposition (September 20 Armed Forces entry); "Travis Airforce Base" and "Camp Lejune" and "Camp Jonson" (Armed Forces entries, likely "Travis Air Force Base", "Camp Lejeune", "Camp Johnson"); "St. Virgen Mary" (October 18 companion-diocese entry, likely "St. Virgin Mary"); the April 5 Anglican Communion line's unusual wording "we pray for the peace of Jerusalem, the people and ministry of The La Iglesia Anglicana de Mexico" (a doubled article, "The La", preserved as printed, alongside an otherwise-unexplained leading "peace of Jerusalem" clause folded into that same subject's name since the source does not separate them into two subjects).

"Calvary Episcopal Church ... in Louisiana" (August 16, 2026) refers to the city of Louisiana, Missouri (a Missouri river town, per the source's own numbering of Missouri congregations by founding year), not the U.S. state of Louisiana named in an earlier, unrelated Armed Forces entry (January 25) -- both are transcribed exactly as printed.

Every date carries the source's own liturgical Sunday label (`liturgicalNote`), transcribed exactly as printed, including its own inconsistent use of a leading "The" (e.g. "Last Sunday after Pentecost" and "First Sunday after Christmas" print with no leading "The", unlike most other weeks).

Built by extracting each quarterly PDF's text with pdftotext -layout (confirmed single-column throughout by rendering and visually checking several pages, including the page containing the one no-place entry above) and manually transcribing each of the 52 weeks against that text.
